failure_patterns.pattern: follow_up_constraint_omission: A new flight-class constraint was ignored, or a new hotel star requirement was incorrectly treated as already satisfied.

rejected_edits.content: - **Interpret clarification answers in context:** Map a short answer to the field or fields the assistant asked about, rather than interpreting an ambiguous word or abbreviation in isolation. Scope a yes/no or restrictive clarification answer to the domain and question asked: for example, “no, only the return flight” changes which flight leg is requested, but does not cancel separately requested hotel or restaurant planning unless the user explicitly withdraws it. An affirmative answer accepting an offered domain or option is a request to proceed. If the reply supplies multiple criteria for one domain, capture all of them and include them together in the same follow-up filter call where supported; do not select only one criterion.
rejected_edits.target: - **Interpret clarification answers in context:** Map a short answer to the field or fields the assistant asked about, rather than interpreting an ambiguous word or abbreviation in isolation. If the reply supplies multiple criteria for one domain, capture all of them and include them together in the same follow-up filter call where supported; do not select only one criterion.

rejected_edits.content: - For flight times, treat “at X” as an exact time range `[X, X]`. For an upper bound such as “by X,” “no later than X,” or “before X,” use `["12:00 AM", X]`; for “after X,” use `[X, "11:59 PM"]`. Preserve the stated AM/PM value.
rejected_edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.

rejected_edits.content: - **Combine known criteria on initial searches:** When no suitable cached base exists and multiple explicit criteria for one domain are already known, include them in the same search call where supported (for example, attraction type and name) rather than searching broadly and then filtering or repeating the search. For hotel searches and filters, map an explicitly stated party size to `num_people` (for example, “solo” means `num_people=1`) and an explicitly stated room count to `num_rooms`. If a follow-up supplies either or both counts, apply all newly supplied count fields together in one same-domain filter on a suitable cached hotel result when needed. Do not infer unspoken counts or pass traveler counts to flight tools.
